a933f90894.q: How does capitated payment work in value-based care models like those used by Kaiser or California Medicaid?
a933f90894.a: In a capitated payment model, a fixed amount is paid to a healthcare provider to assume all costs of care for a patient over a time period. For example, California might pay a healthcare provider $10,000 per year to cover all healthcare costs for a Medicaid patient. If the provider spends less, they keep the excess money; if they spend more, they absorb that cost.

2885899ea3.q: What is the difference between fee-for-service and value-based care payment in healthcare?
2885899ea3.a: Fee-for-service means you provide a service and get paid just for that service with no tie to quality, cost, or outcomes—just straight CPT codes and reimbursements. Value-based care ties the actual payment amount to value, meaning you can earn bonuses for high quality or low-cost care delivery. Value-based care exists on a spectrum from simple care restructuring to full capitated payment models.

97bf2e16f6.q: Can physicians actually earn more money by succeeding in value-based care arrangements?
97bf2e16f6.a: Yes. Physicians who deliver care through value-based care programs and meet their cost and quality benchmarks can earn more than they would through traditional fee-for-service. While there is an initial upfront discount compared to fee-for-service, physicians have access to potential bonus dollars; if they deliver high-quality care at low cost with no readmissions, they can receive more total compensation than under fee-for-service arrangements.

77f619b7aa.q: Why are physicians incentivized to do more in the current RVU-based healthcare system?
77f619b7aa.a: Physicians are incentivized to do more because the current system rewards work through an RVU (Relative Value Unit) system: the more you do, the more you get paid. This is basic behavioral economics—if you incentivize a behavior, more of that behavior will happen. However, the true incentive should be keeping the population healthy, not maximizing volume.

d0ecb5a3bf.q: What percentage margin do not-for-profit health systems in America operate on?
d0ecb5a3bf.a: The average margin of a not-for-profit health system in America is only a little over 1 percent. This slim margin results from decreases in Medicare reimbursements and rising staffing costs due to inflation, making it extremely difficult for hospitals to maintain operations.
